sprigatito: Ørsted's lab raises them in the Botanical Garden glasshouses. They knead warm pavement stones on Nørrebro before curling up for a nap.
floragato: Hides in the hedges of Assistens Kirkegård and pounces on falling leaves. Its vine swings like a skipping rope.
meowscarada: Said to have stolen a rose from every balcony on Strøget in one night. It always leaves the stem behind as a calling card.
charmander: Popular with stall keepers at the Christmas markets, who warm their hands at its tail. It sulks in the November drizzle.
charmeleon: Climbs the chimneys of old Christianshavn to sit in the warm smoke. Chimney sweeps call it a colleague.
charizard: Flies over the Øresund on clear evenings. Ferry passengers say its flame looks like a second sunset.
popplio: Plays in the Islands Brygge harbour baths in summer, balancing beach balls for the swimmers.
brionne: Practises its songs under the bridges, where the echo is best. Kayakers on the canals slow down to listen.
primarina: Its song carries across the whole harbour on still nights. Old sailors in Nyhavn claim it once guided a lost ship home.
eevee: Every family on the block wants one. It changes to suit whoever loves it, the way a city changes its people.
pikachu: Rides in the front box of cargo bikes. It charges the bike lights for free, which makes it very popular with couriers.
pidgey: The most common sight on Copenhagen's squares. It knows exactly which bakery throws out yesterday's rundstykker.
pidgeotto: Patrols the rooftops of Vesterbro and dives on any Rattata that strays from the courtyards.
pidgeot: Glides above the spires on the sea wind. From the top of Rundetårn you can sometimes see one circling the whole city.
lillipup: Its nose finds lost mittens in the snow. Pædagoger in the city's kindergartens bring them on walks.
herdier: Herds children across bike lanes without being asked. Cyclists ring their bells at it in thanks.
stoutland: Its coat is thick enough for a Danish winter on the coast. Fishermen in Dragør used to bring them out on the ice.
wingull: Steals chips from the tables in Nyhavn with perfect timing. Café owners keep water spray bottles for them.
pelipper: Carries post between the harbour islands in its beak. It rarely loses a letter, but it often reads them.
psyduck: Stands in the Lakes and stares at the swans all day. Joggers on the path around Søerne say hello to it every morning.
golduck: Swims the city canals so fast that rowing clubs race against it for practice.
lotad: Floats on the ponds of the Botanical Garden. Children pretend its leaf is a boat.
lombre: Plays tricks on anglers along the Kalvebod shore, tugging lines and then laughing from the reeds.
buneary: Lives in the long grass of the parks. In spring it pops up in the allotment gardens to nibble the first lettuce.
hoothoot: Keeps time for the night buses. Drivers on the Natbus say it hoots at every stop, right on the minute.
noctowl: Watches the city from church towers at night. Its eyes can spot a dropped coin from the top of Rundetårn.
rattata: Lives under the cobbles of Indre By and comes out when the restaurants close. It is not fussy about what it eats.
raticate: Its teeth can chew through a bike lock, so cyclists in Nørrebro never leave their bikes near the drains.
magikarp: Found in every harbour, lake and canal in Copenhagen. Nobody remembers who first threw one into the Lakes.
gyarados: A Gyarados once rose in the harbour mouth and the ferries stopped for a whole day. People still talk about it in Nyhavn.
skwovet: Stuffs its cheeks with berries from the park bushes. It hides the extras in bike baskets and forgets them.
greedent: Waits by the hot dog stands for the end of the day. Some vendors give it the last pølse just to see it smile.
nickit: Sneaks into courtyards at dusk and takes whatever is left outside. It uses its tail to sweep away its tracks.
thievul: Marks the walls of the old town with its scent. Graffiti artists say it has better taste than the city council.
toxel: Babies of this kind gather around the electrical boxes on Nørrebro, sipping the hum of the cables.
toxtricity: Plays loud music in the Vesterbro clubs. If it likes the crowd, the lights in the whole street flicker in time.
combee: Its hives hang under the eaves of the Botanical Garden's glasshouses. The honey is sold at Torvehallerne.
vespiquen: Rules the rooftop beehives of the city. Beekeepers who forget to thank it find their hives empty in the morning.
bounsweet: Smells so sweet that it is often mistaken for a fruit at the markets. Mothers keep them on windowsills for the scent.
steenee: Kicks its way through the garden paths with great pride. Gardeners like it because it chases off bugs.
petilil: Grows in the flower beds of the Botanical Garden. Tea brewed from its leaf is a cure for a long night out.
cutiefly: Follows flowers from balcony to balcony all summer. A Nørrebro balcony with no Cutiefly is a sad one.
ribombee: Rolls pollen into little balls that it trades with other Pokémon. It is a regular at the garden's café terrace.
smoliv: Arrived on a ship from the south and took a liking to the sunny side of the Palm House.
dolliv: Its oil keeps the old hinges of the Palm House doors from squeaking.
arboliva: A few live in the warmest corner of the Botanical Garden. Locals bring bread to dip in the oil it shares.
spinarak: Spins webs across the iron railings of the canals. In the morning frost they look like lace.
ariados: Hunts in the dark of the old cemeteries. It never harms the visitors, but it watches them closely.
oddish: Walks around the Lakes at night and plants itself somewhere new each dawn. Gardeners find it in odd places.
gloom: The smell is bad, but the city's foxes stay away from gardens where it lives, so gardeners put up with it.
grimer: Comes up from the steam tunnels under the city when it rains. It feeds on what the drains carry.
muk: Lived in the old harbour sludge before the clean-up. Some went quiet when the water got clean, waiting.
zubat: Flocks in the tunnels under Copenhagen. Tunnel workers on the metro have a song about them.
golbat: Swoops through the old fort's casemates at night. The bite is sharp but rarely dangerous.
trubbish: Lives in the bins of the busiest streets. It is much happier since the city started sorting its rubbish.
garbodor: Builds a home in the city dumps. Workers at CopenHill say it likes to ride the ski slope on the roof.
starly: Flocks of hundreds wheel over the Kalvebod marshes in autumn, a sight people come out to watch.
staravia: Fights with Wingull over the best bench in the harbour. Neither ever gives up.
staraptor: Hunts above the fields of Amager. Farmers welcome it because it keeps the Rattata away.
wattrel: Rides the sea wind over the wind farm at Middelgrunden and naps on the turbine blades.
kilowattrel: Stores charge from storms over the Øresund. Vanguard engineers tried to tag them and lost every tag.
murkrow: Gathers on the church roofs of Indre By. It collects shiny things, and the Trinitatis loft is full of them.
tentacool: Drifts into the harbour on warm summers. Swimmers at the harbour baths keep an eye out for it.
tentacruel: Large groups gather off Trekroner when the water warms. Sailors take the long way round.
finizen: Races the harbour buses across the water. It is the fastest swimmer in Copenhagen's canals.
palafin: Only shows its hero form when a friend is in trouble. Lifeguards at Amager Strand love it.
shellos: Lines the stones of the harbour walls. Its colour depends on which side of the Sound it was born.
gastrodon: Crawls up the jetties of Dragør at low tide. Children leave it the crusts of their sandwiches.
machop: Helps the movers who carry pianos up five floors of narrow Copenhagen stairs.
machoke: Works the cranes at the shipyards. Dock workers say one Machoke is worth three trucks.
mareanie: Clings to the piles under the harbour piers. Its spikes have spoiled many a fisherman's net.
toxapex: Builds a dome of spikes in the cold water of the fort. Even Gyarados keep their distance.
rolycoly: Rolls along the old railway tracks of Kødbyen, where the coal trains once ran.
carkol: Stokes the ovens of old bakeries. Some bakers in Vesterbro still keep one by the stove.
coalossal: Once powered the city's coal plants. Now that the chimneys are cold, it is looking for work.
hoppip: Floats over the parks on the summer breeze. When it blows from the sea, they all drift inland together.
skiploom: Its flower opens in the sun on Frederiksberg's lawns. Picnickers use them to tell the time.
jumpluff: Rides the jet stream far out over the sea. Some say a few reach the Faroe Islands.
shroodle: Paints its marks on the walls of Superkilen. The murals there are partly its work.
grafaiai: Signs the walls of Nørrebro with its own poison paint. Tariq calls it the best artist in the neighbourhood.
stunky: Digs under garden sheds in the allotments. Allotment holders have opinions about it.
skuntank: Its smell can clear a whole street. Bike thieves in Christiania learned to stay away from its den.
smeargle: Paints on the canvas walls of Christiania. Every Smeargle's mark is a little different.
pawmi: Sparks between the paving stones after a storm. Children chase them through puddles.
pawmo: Gives friends a shock with its paw to cheer them up. It is very popular at the Bakken amusement park.
pawmot: Its fur stands on end before a storm. Sailors watch it to know when to bring the boats in.
greavard: Lives in the oldest corners of Assistens Kirkegård. It brings a lantern to anyone who gets lost after dark.
houndstone: Sleeps on old gravestones. The poets buried in the cemetery are said to have their own Houndstone.
magnemite: Clings to the power lines over the railway yards. It hums along with the trains.
magneton: Gathers around Vanguard's substations. Electricians in the city count them like birds.
klink: Its gears spin in time with the old clocks of Børsen. The merchants once used it to keep the hour.
klang: Turns the wheels of the drawbridges. Knippelsbro's bridge keepers used to keep one in the control booth.
klinklang: Runs the last old machines on Refshaleøen. Its gears grind slower every year.
voltorb: Looks just like a Poké Ball. Pokémon Center nurses have learned to check every ball before picking it up.
electrode: Explodes when it gets too much charge. Lightning storms over Amager set off whole groups.
tadbulb: Lights up the shallow water of the Lakes at night. Couples walk around Søerne to see it glow.
kricketot: Plays a gentle tune in the meadows of Dyrehaven in summer. The deer don't mind.
kricketune: Its song fills the summer nights at Bakken. Some say the fairground music borrowed its melody.
jigglypuff: Sings at the cafés on Strøget. Customers fall asleep in their coffee and the waiters wake them for the bill.
vulpix: Its tails keep it warm through a Danish winter. Families in the old town once kept them as hearth companions.
natu: Sits on the statues of the old town and stares at people. It is said to know what will happen tomorrow.
xatu: Stands on the top of Rundetårn watching the stars and the city. Astronomers swear it can predict the weather.
ralts: Senses the feelings of the people around it. It is drawn to Copenhagen's happiest households.
kirlia: Dances in the little squares of Indre By in the evening light. Street musicians play for it.
gardevoir: Protects its trainer at any cost. Some say one stood guard over the Little Mermaid one stormy night.
joltik: Feeds on the hum of old fuse boxes in Vesterbro's back stairs. A blown fuse is often its fault.
galvantula: Strings electric webs across the abandoned halls of Refshaleøen. The workers who are left wear rubber boots.
mankey: Fights pigeons for crusts on the benches of Kongens Have. It always wins and is never satisfied.
primeape: Gets so angry it forgets why. The rowers on the Lakes keep a wide berth.
carvanha: Swarms in the deep harbour channels. Divers who work on the bridges watch for them.
sharpedo: Can cross the Øresund in minutes. Ferries have reported seeing one racing them to Malmø.
croagunk: Hangs about the saunas of the harbour baths and croaks at the cold-water swimmers.
toxicroak: Its poison claws can stop a fight before it starts. Bouncers in Kødbyen are glad to have one.
crabrawler: Climbs the ropes of the old ships in Nyhavn to box with the sea breeze.
poliwag: Its swirl can be seen through the clear water of the harbour. Children try to copy the pattern.
poliwhirl: Lives in the reed beds along Kalvebod. Its belly swirl hypnotises the frogs.
lilligant: Grows in the finest flower beds of Frederiksberg Have. The gardeners there say it trims itself.
porygon: Made by programmers in a lab out on the harbour. Copies of it still turn up in the Pokédex servers.
qwilfishhisui: A northern Qwilfish that sailors brought back from colder seas. Captain Freja's crew swear by it.
flittle: Bounces around the sandy edges of Amager Fælled. It doesn't fly, but it can hover for a moment.
espathra: Struts through the meadows of Amager Fælled. Its glowing eyes can stop a runner in their tracks.
snorunt: Shows up in Copenhagen only in hard winters. Children leave out bowls of snow for it.
glalie: Freezes the edges of the harbour in a cold snap. Ice skaters on the Lakes thank it.
cetoddle: Came down from the north in a cold winter and never left. It lives near Kødbyen's cold stores.
cryogonal: Forms in the freezer halls of Kødbyen. On cold nights it drifts out into the white-tiled square.
spheal: Rolls along the harbour ice in winter. When there is no ice, it rolls along the harbour baths instead.
sealeo: Balances beach balls on its nose for crowds on Langelinie. It is happiest with an audience.
walrein: Lies on the breakwater at Trekroner like a sack of stones. Its tusks are older than the fort.
cubchoo: Its runny nose freezes into icicles. Kasper's kitchen staff keep one to chill the drinks.
beartic: Swims in the freezing water off Refshaleøen in winter. It is the only one who enjoys it.
bergmite: Grows on the walls of the cold stores. Workers knock it off and it grows right back.
avalugg: Big enough to carry a group of Bergmite across the harbour on its back.
wooloo: Rolls down the slopes of the deer park. Its wool is used to knit the warmest Danish jumpers.
dubwool: Butts heads with its rivals in the fields north of the city. The farmers bet on the winners.
mudbray: Hauls carts for the farmers on Amager. It loves to roll in the mud after the rain.
mudsdale: Its hooves can split stone. The builders of Copenhagen's old ramparts used them to haul earth.
bramblin: Blows along the empty lots in the wind. Some cross the whole of Amager Fælled in one gust.
brambleghast: Wraps itself around lonely bus shelters on windy nights. Nobody knows what it's waiting for.
litwick: Sits on graves in Assistens Kirkegård. People leave candles, and it is not always clear which is which.
lampent: Swings through the old streets at night like a lantern. Some say it guided Andersen home.
gastly: Drifts through the cemetery walls after dark. It makes the hair on visitors' necks stand up.
haunter: Hides in the shadows of the old town and taps people on the shoulder. Then it laughs.
misdreavus: Moans in the cellars of old Christianshavn. The owners call it the house's oldest tenant.
sinistea: Lives in an old teacup in an antique shop on Ravnsborggade. Buyers are often surprised.
phantump: Haunts the oldest trees of Dyrehaven. The forest wardens say it is a lost child's spirit.
wooper: Wanders out of the Lakes on rainy mornings and sits on the footpath. Joggers step around it.
quagsire: Floats in the moat of Kastellet with its mouth open, letting the fish swim in.
fidough: Lives in the warm back rooms of bakeries. Birthe at Bageriet says it helps the dough rise.
dachsbun: Smells like fresh bread. Danish bakers say a bakery without one doesn't smell right.
chandelure: Hangs in the old chandeliers of the palaces. When it is pleased, the whole ballroom glows.
mismagius: Its chants echo in the empty churches at night. Bell ringers have heard it humming along.
sableye: Lives in the dark under Søndermarken, where it eats the gems in the cistern walls.
dewpider: Carries a bubble of water on its head so it can breathe on dry land. Common in the cisterns.
araquanid: Its water bubble can hold a child. It is gentle, but it does not like visitors in its cistern.
rotom: Moves into old appliances and gives them a new life. Ørsted's Pokédex has a Rotom inside.
deerling: The fawns of Dyrehaven follow the deer herds. Its coat changes colour with the seasons.
sawsbuck: Leads the herds of Dyrehaven. Its antlers bloom with flowers each spring.
fletchling: Sings from the tops of the street lamps along Strandvejen. Its call means morning has come.
fletchinder: Hunts insects over the fields by Lyngby. The embers on its wings glow in the dusk.
talonflame: Dives on its prey at incredible speed. It has been clocked faster than the S-train.
pikipek: Drums on the old wooden ships in Nyhavn. The boat owners are not happy about it.
trumbeak: Stores berries in its beak and spits them at those who annoy it, mostly Wingull.
toucannon: Its beak heats up to cook the seeds inside. It has a stall at Torvehallerne, unofficially.
noibat: Lives in the casemates of the old forts. Its screech makes the stones ring.
noivern: Guards the harbour forts at night. Its ultrasound can be felt on the ferries out of Nordhavn.
phanpy: Plays in the mud by the Kalvebod shore. It sprays water at anyone who looks hot.
donphan: Can knock down a wall by rolling into it. It was used to clear the old shipyards.
pancham: Tries to look tough on the street corners of Nørrebro. The leaf in its mouth is a mint leaf.
pangoro: Settles fights in the Kødbyen clubs. Nobody argues with it twice.
skiddo: Grazes on the grass roofs of new buildings. Its back sprouts a leaf that tells it the weather.
gogoat: Carries hikers through Dyrehaven. It knows every path in the forest.
porygon2: An upgraded Porygon made in the harbour labs. Vanguard has tried to buy the patent many times.
bronzor: Found buried under Slotsholmen. Archaeologists think it was made in the city's earliest days.
bronzong: Hangs in the old bell towers like a bell. When it rings, rain follows.
raichu: Lights up a whole street of cargo bike lamps with one tail swish.
jolteon: Its fur bristles with charge. In a thunderstorm, the street lights of Østerbro dim around it.
magnezone: Gathers where the grid is strongest. It can feel when the city's power is drained.
bellibolt: Sits in the harbour shallows and glows. Children at Islands Brygge have named every one of them.
espurr: Has psychic power strong enough to knock over a teacup. It lives in the cafés of Frederiksberg.
meowstic: Keeps its ears folded to hide its power. Students at the university keep them as study companions.
drowzee: Eats bad dreams. Hospital wards in Copenhagen are glad to see one walk past.
hypno: Swings its pendulum on the night trains. Commuters fall asleep before Østerport.
staryu: Washes up on Amager Strand at night and glows like a beached star.
starmie: Its core shines in colours that reflect the harbour lights. Sailors use it as a lighthouse.
stantler: Roams the forests north of the city. Its antlers bend the air into strange shapes.
wyrdeer: An old kind of deer said to have roamed the island before the city was built.
clauncher: Shoots water from its claw at the crabs on the harbour piers.
clawitzer: Fires water strong enough to knock a Pidgey off a roof. It lives under Knippelsbro.
buizel: Swims in the harbour like a sea otter. It loves the water bus routes.
floatzel: Rescues tired swimmers at the harbour baths. Lifeguards say it is their best colleague.
shellder: Clamps onto the anchors of the boats in Nyhavn. Taking it off is a two-person job.
impidimp: Steals from the stalls at Bakken and laughs at the angry owners.
morgrem: Talks people into foolish bets at the Bakken amusement park. It always wins.
grimmsnarl: Its hair forms muscles that it uses to bully other Pokémon. The fairground guards fear it.
morelull: Glows softly on the forest floor of Dyrehaven at night. Hikers follow the lights.
shiinotic: Its spores make travellers sleepy. Many a hiker in Dyrehaven has woken up miles off the path.
mimikyu: Wears a costume made to look like Pikachu. Children at Bakken leave it presents.
slurpuff: Can smell the sweetest treats from across the city. It lives above a bakery in Vesterbro.
swirlix: Eats nothing but sugar. Its fur is as sweet as candyfloss at the Bakken stands.
mrmime: Performs on Strøget in the summer. It builds invisible walls and charges people to walk through them.
mrrime: Tap-dances on the frozen Lakes. Its moustache stays frozen all winter.
glimmet: Grows in the deep caves under the city. Its crystals glow in the dark.
glimmora: Scatters poisonous crystals over the old harbour. Divers keep away from its nests.
flabebe: Floats among the flowers of Frederiksberg Have. Each one picks its flower for life.
floette: Tends the flower boxes of the city's balconies. Grandparents swear it keeps them in bloom.
spritzee: Its scent was a favourite of the royal court in the old palace. Perfumers still study it.
togepi: Said to bring luck to anyone who hatches it. Many Copenhagen families keep a Togepi egg in the attic.
togetic: Flies over the homes of kind people. It is often seen above the old almshouses.
marill: Plays in the Lakes on hot days. Its tail floats like a beach ball.
azumarill: Lives in the clearest water of the harbour. It can hear a fish move from across the canal.
hatenna: Feels the feelings of people near it. Busy streets like Strøget give it a headache.
hattrem: Beats anything that disturbs its calm. The quiet reading rooms of the library suit it.
hatterene: Lives in the deepest woods of Dyrehaven. Its psychic power can tear apart a tree.
clefairy: Gathers on moonlit nights in the castle gardens. The guards keep its secret.
wigglytuff: Its fur is so soft that the palace once used it to fill pillows.
mimejr: Copies the people around it. Street performers in Indre By are often upstaged by one.
electivire: Its tails crackle with power. It turns up near Vanguard's works when the voltage spikes.
hariyama: Pushes stalled cars off the bridges. It once moved a bus at rush hour.
lucario: Can read the aura of people around it. Guards at the palace walk the grounds with one.
luxray: Can see through walls. Police in Copenhagen use it to find lost children.
houndoom: Its howl at night chills the old town. Superstitious locals close their shutters.
manectric: Lives near the power lines on the edge of the city. Its mane gathers static from the air.
bisharp: Leads groups of Pawniard in the alleys of Slotsholmen. Nobody walks there alone.
corviknight: Carries people across the city like a taxi. Its steel feathers ring in the wind.
corvisquire: Perches on the green copper roofs of Slotsholmen and watches the tourists.
copperajah: Its skin turns green like the city's copper roofs as it grows old.
cufant: Carries heavy loads at the harbour. Its copper skin shines when it is new.
duraludon: Its body is as hard as the steel beams of the new harbour buildings. It likes tall places.
skarmory: Nests on the cranes at the shipyards. Its steel feathers are sharp as knives.
pawniard: Gathers in packs on Slotsholmen. Its blades are said to be sharper than the city's politicians.
probopass: Its nose always points north. The ferry captains of the Sound trust it more than a compass.
torkoal: Kept by the archives of Slotsholmen to warm the reading rooms. It puffs out smoke when content.
ditto: Copies the shape of anything it sees. A few have been found pretending to be statues on Strøget.
machamp: Unloads whole container ships at Nordhavn by hand. The crane drivers sometimes just watch.
gurdurr: Carries steel beams around the Refshaleøen shipyards. It never puts its beam down, even to eat.
conkeldurr: Taught the first shipwrights of Copenhagen to mix concrete, or so the dock workers say.
durant: Marches through the empty hulls of the drydock in long lines. Its jaws can bite through rivets.
boldore: Found in the gravel heaps by the old shipyard. Its crystals glow orange when it is upset.
crobat: Flies through the steam tunnels so fast it hardly makes a sound. Tunnel workers see only a shadow.
luxio: Its claws spark when it is excited. It patrols the cable runs under the harbour.
heliolisk: Spreads its frill to soak up the sun on CopenHill's roof. On grey days it sulks inside the plant.
zebstrika: Gallops along the quay when a storm rolls in from the Sound. Lightning seems to follow it.
steelix: Coils around the foundations of the great crane. Engineers say it is the only thing holding it up.
kingdra: Sleeps at the bottom of the harbour mouth. When it stirs, the ferries rock.
haxorus: Its tusks can cut through ship's steel. The welders at the shipyard leave it their scrap.
excadrill: Dug half the tunnels for the new metro line before the machines arrived, the old miners claim.
metang: Floats over the shipyards, welding two minds into one. It hums like a transformer.
metagross: Its four brains work faster than the computers at Vanguard. It does not trust them either.
porygonz: A Porygon someone tried to make smarter in a lab on the harbour. It now acts very strangely.
vikavolt: Fires electric beams from its jaws. CopenHill's engineers use it to test the lines.
